claims.reason: The proof uses `[QuasiCompact f]` only through `Hom.ker_apply` (Basic.lean:701), which is the one lemma here that needs it. Nothing else in the statement refers to it: `f.ker` and `.radical` are defined for any morphism. I checked the alternative proof against Mathlib. `Hom.ker f` is defined as `ofIdeals fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom` (line 691). `le_ofIdeals_iff : I ≤ ofIdeals J ↔ I.ideal ≤ J` exists at line 124. `Hom.ideal_ker_le` (line 694) gives `f.ker.ideal U ≤ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom` without quasi-compactness. `le_radical` exists at line 535. `radical` is built from `(I.ideal U).radical` (line 511), and the original proof already uses `radical_ideal`. The `≥` direction is `le_radical`. For `≤`, apply `le_ofIdeals_iff.mpr` (allowed because `f.ker` unfolds to `ofIdeals`). For each affine open U, `(f.ker.ideal U).radical ≤ (RingHom.ker _).radical` holds by `Ideal.radical_mono` applied to `ideal_ker_le`. The right side equals `RingHom.ker _`, because that kernel is `comap` of `⊥` and `⊥` is radical in the reduced ring Γ(X, f⁻¹ᵁ U). This is the same `Ideal.isRadical_bot.comap` step the original proof uses, with the same `IsReduced` instance on sections. No step needs quasi-compactness, so the statement holds for every morphism f from a reduced scheme.
